executivePulse.interpretation: Memory and AI infrastructure remain under high pressure. Server DRAM, DRAM and HBM are currently among the most constrained areas. New capacity and improved yields can provide relief, but will reach the market only with a lag. For buyers, supply security, alternative BOMs and early procurement remain critical.

signals.title: Apple reportedly close to deploying CXMT DRAM alongside SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron
signals.summary: Reports suggest Apple is considering using CXMT DRAM in addition to supplies from SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron.
signals.analysis: This report is relevant to datacentre storage: it could affect prices, available capacity and procurement strategies for enterprise SSDs.

signals.title: Samsung HBM4 yield rises to 80% — ahead of year‑end target
signals.summary: Reports indicate Samsung's HBM4 yield has climbed to 80%, achieving the year‑end target early.
signals.analysis: Higher HBM yields can accelerate the ramp of new AI accelerators and free up more HBM capacity in the medium term. Crucial is whether the yield improvement is visible in production volumes and shipped modules.

signals.title: SK Hynix faces US patent dispute over HBM and 3D NAND
signals.summary: Reports indicate SK Hynix faces a potential patent dispute in the United States concerning HBM and 3D NAND.
signals.analysis: HBM remains a central bottleneck for AI accelerators. Changes to production, qualification or demand will directly affect available GPU systems and pricing in the AI infrastructure market.
